[[Image:Medinilla magnifica flor.jpg|thumb|''Medinilla magnifica'' is a popular ornamental plant endemic to the Luzon, Mindoro and Panay islands]]
'''''Medinilla''''' is a large paleotropical genus of about 370 species of [[flowering plant]]s in the family [[Melastomataceae]], native to tropical regions of the Old World from Africa east through southeast Asia to Australia and the western Pacific Ocean. The genus was named after [[José de Medinilla y Pineda]], governor of the [[Mariana Islands]] in 1820.{{R|POWO}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 December 2020 |title=Notes on the Medinilla (Melastomataceae) of Palawan, Philippines, Including Two New Species: M. simplicymosa and M. ultramaficola |url=https://bioone.org/journals/systematic-botany/volume-45/issue-4/036364420X16033962925376/Notes-on-the-Medinilla-Melastomataceae-of-Palawan-Philippines-Including-Two/10.1600/036364420X16033962925376.short |url-status=live |access-date=3 April 2026 |website=BioOne}}</ref>

Species in this genus are [[evergreen]] shrubs or vines. The leaves are opposite or whorled, or alternate in some species. The flowers are white, pink, red, or orange, and are produced singly or in large [[panicle]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Medinilla {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/medinilla/ |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}}</ref>Certain Medinilla species have high economic value as they are used in medicinal and ornamental applications. <ref>{{Cite web |date=2024 |title=The effect of shade and drought on the growth and proline content of Medinilla speciosa and Medinilla verrucosa plants |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1755-1315/1362/1/012061 |url-status=live |access-date=3 April 2026 |website=IOPScience}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025 |title=The immunomodulatory activity of parijoto fruit (Medinilla speciosa) fraction against phagocytosis macrophages and lymphocyte proliferation |url=https://journals.lww.com/japtr/fulltext/2025/01000/the_immunomodulatory_activity_of_parijoto_fruit.2.aspx |access-date=3 April 2026 |website=Journal of Advanced Pharmaceutical Technology & Research}}</ref>
